transcript.text: We had a power cut last night and now our Candy washer dryer is completely dead - no lights, nothing. Everything else in the house came back on. The plug fuse is fine, I swapped it. Help!

Here's a step-by-step checklist, starting with the easiest and most likely fixes.

## 1. Check the power is actually reaching the machine
• Test the socket. Plug something else (a kettle or lamp) into the same socket. Sockets can fail on their own, especially after a surge.
• Check for a switched fused spur. Many kitchens have a separate switch above the worktop for the washer, often labelled "washing machine". Make sure it's on. If it has its own fuse (a little slot on the faceplate), that fuse may have blown too.
• Check your consumer unit (fuse box). Even if the lights and other sockets work, an individual breaker (MCB) or one bank of the RCD can trip. Look for any switch that's down or in a middle position and push it fully off, then back on.
• Avoid extension leads. If the machine is on one, plug it directly into the wall to test.

## 2. Do a hard reset
Electronics can sometimes lock up after an abrupt power loss.
1. Turn the machine's dial/button off.
2. Unplug it (or switch off at the spur) and leave it for 10-15 minutes.
3. Plug back in, turn it on, and try again.

## 3. Check the plug and cable
• With it unplugged, open the plug and check the wires are secure. Make sure the new fuse is the right rating (normally 13A for a washer dryer).
• Look along the mains cable for any damage or scorch marks.

## 4. If it's still completely dead
If the socket is live and the reset didn't help, the power cut (or the surge when power came back) has most likely damaged a component. Common culprits:
• Mains interference suppressor/filter: a small part where the power cable enters the machine. It often fails after surges, and it's a cheap, fairly common repair.
• Main control board (PCB): a more expensive repair.

Please don't open the machine yourself unless you're competent with electrical repairs. Internal parts can hold a charge even when unplugged.

## 5. Before paying for a repair
• Warranty: If it's fairly new, contact Candy (Haier/Candy customer service) or check any extended warranty.
• Home insurance: Many policies cover power surge damage or accidental damage to appliances. It's worth a call.
• Power cut compensation: If the outage was caused by your network operator, call 105 (the free UK power cut line) to report it and ask about compensation for damaged appliances. Keep any repair reports or receipts.

If you tell me what you find at the socket and fuse box, I can help narrow it down further.

Tried most of that. The socket works (a lamp runs fine in it), the new 13A fuse made no difference, and the consumer unit has everything switched on. I also unplugged it for over 10 minutes and it's still dead. The plug and cable look fine. I'm not sure about a separate spur switch. Might it still be under an extended warranty? I think it has 3 years but I'm not certain.

Since a lamp works in the same socket the washer dryer plugs into, you can rule out the spur switch. If the socket has power, any spur feeding it is on. That means you've now ruled out everything outside the machine, so the fault is almost certainly internal (most likely the suppressor/filter or the control board). That's a job for an engineer, ideally one you don't have to pay for.

## Finding out if it's under warranty

1. Get the model and serial number
Look on the sticker around the inside rim of the door opening, or sometimes on the back. You'll need these for any claim.

2. Check your records
• Candy registration: If you registered the machine when you bought it, you may have a confirmation email from Candy (or Haier, their parent company) showing any extended warranty. Search your inbox for "Candy" or "Haier".
• Retailer care plan: If you bought it from somewhere like Currys, AO, or Argos, check whether you took out a care/repair plan. The receipt or your online account should show it.
• Proof of purchase: Dig out the receipt or order confirmation. They'll want the purchase date.

3. Contact Candy directly
Go through the Candy UK website's support/repair booking section or call their customer service. Give them the serial number and they can tell you exactly what cover it has.

Heads-up: Manufacturer warranties sometimes exclude damage caused by power surges. Describe the fault honestly ("completely dead after a power cut"), but if they decline on those grounds, see the options below.

## If it's not covered

• Home insurance: Many policies cover accidental damage or electrical surge damage to appliances. Check your policy or call your insurer.
• Consumer Rights Act 2015: If it's only a few years old, you may have a claim against the retailer (not Candy) on the basis that it hasn't lasted a reasonable time. You can raise this up to six years after purchase, though the older it is, the harder it is to argue.
• Your electricity network operator: If the power cut or the surge when power returned damaged appliances, you can sometimes claim from the local network operator (not your energy supplier). Report it. Neighbours with damaged electronics would strengthen the case.

If you can find the model number or purchase date, I can help you work out which route looks most promising.
